summary: Iter 17 verification complete. New POST /api/public/signup-salon endpoint fully validated across 7 scenarios (happy path, auth-after-signup, duplicate email 400, weak password 422, invalid slug 400, slug auto-uniqueness, rate limit 429) — all pass when run with a clean rate-limit bucket. Full regression suite across iter7/10/11/13/15/16/17 = 60 passed, 1 skipped (pre-existing tenant2 isolation), 1 environmental failure caused by in-memory rate-limit bucket pollution across the iter17 test session (NOT a code bug — verified independently). Frontend smoke: all 3 logins (admin, super-admin, elegance owner) succeed and land on correct dashboards; /reports renders Recent Invoices + Commission card; /pos renders full POS UI; public /book/miracurl-marathahalli renders the 5-step wizard; Emergent badge correctly hidden via CSS.

minor.issue: Rate-limit bucket is in-memory (module-level _RATE_BUCKET) and shared per-process. After a single batch test run, the IP gets stuck for 900s. Pragmatic: ok for prod; for tests, requires backend restart between batched runs. Consider Redis or per-test eviction hook for testability.

issues: Reports uses browser-native <input type='date'> for From/To pickers instead of a shadcn Calendar component — minor UX inconsistency with the rest of the app.

action_items: None — iter17 endpoint and all prior regressions are green. No bugs to fix.

(Optional, low priority) Document in test_iter17 that the rate-limit test will pollute the in-memory bucket for 15 minutes; subsequent iter17 runs need a `sudo supervisorctl restart backend` to reset. Alternatively, add a hidden /api/_test/reset-ratelimit endpoint guarded by a test-only flag.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py /public/signup-salon: solid implementation — uses Pydantic for input validation, slugify+_SLUG_RE for slug safety, unique-slug loop capped at 50 attempts, status='trial' + trial_end_date=+7d, JWT issued and cookies set so user is auto-logged-in. No issues.

server.py:182 _RATE_BUCKET is process-local — won't survive a backend restart and won't be consistent across multiple uvicorn workers if scaled. Acceptable for current single-worker preview, but flag for production scale-out.
server.py:537 trial_end is stored as date.isoformat() (string), while DB convention elsewhere uses datetime.isoformat() — minor inconsistency, harmless.
Pre-existing console warnings (chart width(-1), <span> child of <option> hydration warning) are cosmetic — unchanged from iter16.
Strongly recommend extracting the in-memory rate-limit to Redis before going to production (multi-worker, multi-instance) — current impl will allow N-times-N-workers signups.

success_rate.frontend: 100% (admin dashboard, super-admin tabs, elegance dashboard, public booking 5-step wizard, /reports cards, /pos full UI, Emergent badge hidden — all verified)

context_for_next_testing_agent: Iter 17 added POST /api/public/signup-salon only (no UI). To re-run iter17 backend tests cleanly: `sudo supervisorctl restart backend && export REACT_APP_BACKEND_URL=https://hair-hub-system.preview.emergentagent.com && python -m pytest backend/tests/test_iter17_signup_salon.py -n 0 -v`. The slug_auto_uniqueness + rate_limit tests share the in-memory bucket so the batch must start fresh. Full regression: same restart, then run all 7 test files with `-n 0` (xdist breaks iter13 module-state; addopts in pytest.ini forces -n 2 so you MUST override with -n 0). iter18 will likely add the /signup-salon frontend wizard — when it appears, smoke-test it at /signup-salon and verify it POSTs to /api/public/signup-salon and stores access_token in localStorage.
rca of the issue: The single test failure (test_signup_slug_auto_uniqueness) in batched runs is NOT a code bug. Root cause: the iter17 test session makes 5+ successful signups before slug_auto runs, exhausting the in-memory _RATE_BUCKET which is hardcoded at limit=4 per 900s in server.py:519. Backend restart clears the bucket and slug_auto passes cleanly (verified twice). The /public/signup-salon endpoint itself is fully correct: slug='my-new-salon' is generated from salon_name, and a second signup with the identical name correctly produces 'my-new-salon-2' via the suffix loop. Mitigation already applied: added test-file-level comment documenting the rate-limit caveat; recommended longer-term: move rate-limit to Redis or expose a test-only reset endpoint.
